source.title: Large-Batch Training for LSTM and Beyond
source.authors: Yang You; Jonathan Hseu; Chris Ying; J. Demmel; K. Keutzer; Cho-Jui Hsieh

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether increasing batch size harms held-out task performance under a different training recipe: linear-epoch gradual warmup with square-root learning-rate scaling.
record.gate_note: Reports batch-size comparisons for LSTM and ResNet-50 task metrics. The paper's statements about prior work are not extracted as results. Figure-only comparisons with Adam and comprehensive tuning are included only where the text describes the outcome; precise figure values are not recoverable.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out performance across batch sizes with an adapted learning-rate and warmup recipe at fixed epoch budgets, testing V5's recipe-adaptation clause. Its momentum-versus-Adam comparisons on MNIST and PTB-small also bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate as a statement of the authors' conclusion: square-root learning-rate scaling with warmup epochs proportional to batch size enables up to 64-fold LSTM batch scaling and ResNet-50 batches of 32768 while maintaining accuracy. Their claim of constant performance allows small numerical differences in the tables.
record.recipe_differences: Uses large-batch training with a different warmup schedule and square-root learning-rate scaling; tested on LSTM tasks and ResNet-50 ImageNet. The paper also compares LEGW with Adam and other tuning schemes.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the required warmup length and learning rate under LEGW; the paper reports task results varying by batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: GNMT retains BLEU above the 21.8 reference baseline through batch 4096; within LEGW, BLEU is 22.7 at batch 256 and 22.2 at batch 4096 after two epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate scaling and batch-dependent warmup can preserve useful held-out translation quality with larger batches at fixed epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: LEGW outperforms tuned Adam on GNMT and PTB-large, but these rows do not establish the specified SGD comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch recipe choice affects held-out performance relative to tuned Adam.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several LSTM batch-size comparisons are available only in figures, with exact values not stated in the text. The large-batch results use an adapted recipe, so they do not isolate batch size under a fixed recipe.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible separately reported results omitted. Comparisons whose exact values are only in figures are recorded as figure-only rows where the text states their qualitative outcome.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Training-performance comparisons, broad hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers. PTB-large uses LARS rather than the specified SGD comparator.

The large-batch penalty under an unchanged recipe, its workload-dependent onset, and normalization or regularization interventions. The study primarily tests recovery through learning-rate scaling and warmup.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap correlations, and ranking against alternative measures.

missing.what: Separate held-out optimizer-comparison rows for momentum with LEGW versus tuned Adam on MNIST and PTB-small. Existing sweep rows mention these comparisons but do not encode their comparator or outcome separately.
PTB-large's batch-20 versus batch-640 held-out perplexity comparison at 55 epochs. R6 instead records superiority to Adam; the text reports lossless scaling but exact figure values are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Supports for V5 concern its explicit adaptation clause, not evidence that an unchanged recipe incurs a penalty. The record incorrectly says no fixed-epoch language-model comparison is reported: PTB-small and PTB-large are language models. Exact plotted values and uncertainty estimates are unavailable.

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares LEGW with Adam on task performance, but does not report a comparison that isolates adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the version's stated tuning conditions.
No language-model batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget is reported; the paper reports LSTM task metrics and ImageNet classification. Its recipe changes with batch size.
Dropout and its interaction with weight decay or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
